headline: Jay Clayton, the US intelligence chief, is to lead a new White House AI task force with 120 days to report on the technology's risks.
score_reason: A new top-level AI policy body for the US government with named members and a deadline; the appointment is reported, not yet formally announced.
importance_line: The US now routes its AI policy through its intelligence chief and a 120-day review built to avoid 'overregulation', which shapes the rules every American and every AI company will live under, though the appointment is still only reported.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, as relayed by Reuters and AFP, that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will serve as the administration's AI czar and chair a 'Super Intelligence Force' that has 120 days to deliver findings on AI risks, with Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent among its members. The appointment itself was first reported on Friday 3 Oct 2026; the new detail is the charter, which asks the group to review existing law, how AI breaches and jailbreaks are reported to government, and how to respond to AI threats "while preventing overregulation and regulatory capture", while the White House has not yet formally confirmed the appointment.
notes: Follow-up of 1003:C13-08. Original Reuters link blocked (401); text read from Scripps News and Turkiye Today (AFP), both crediting the WSJ, which is the source.
